precepts.text: Peter walked on the water, but as soon as doubt came he began to sink; had the priests doubted and thought the water was about to fall, they could not have stood, but their feet stood firm.
precepts.point: The priests stayed firm at their post in the riverbed even after all the people had passed over, until the Lord spake to Joshua and Joshua gave the order: come ye up out of Jordan. That is discipline, order, fortitude, and faith; they held their place in the midst of a stopped river without wavering.
precepts.why:
The priests stayed firm at their post in the riverbed even after all the people had passed over, until the Lord spake to Joshua and Joshua gave the order, “Come ye up out of Jordan.” Compare Peter. “And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus. But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me.” Christ caught him and said, “O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?”

Peter walked on the water, but as soon as doubt came he began to sink. Had the priests doubted and thought the water was about to fall, they could not have stood; but their feet stood firm in the midst of a stopped river without wavering. That is discipline, order, fortitude, and faith. And everything held its place exactly as long as Israel needed it to: only when the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up unto the dry land did the waters of Jordan return unto their place and flow over all his banks as before.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: When all the people were clean passed over, the Lord commanded Joshua to take twelve men, one out of every tribe, and have each carry a stone upon his shoulder out of the midst of Jordan, from the very place where the priests' feet stood firm, over to the lodging place.

The stones are a sign and a memorial: when your children ask their fathers in time to come, What mean ye by these stones? ye shall answer them, that the waters of Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. These stones lay in the middle of a river that Israel walked through on dry ground, and they memorialize that forever.
Joshua also set up twelve stones in the midst of Jordan itself, in the place where the feet of the priests which bare the ark stood, and they are there unto this day.
The priests which bare the ark stood in the midst of Jordan until every thing was finished that the Lord commanded Joshua to speak unto the people, and the people hasted and passed over.

The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh passed over armed before the children of Israel, about forty thousand prepared for war, keeping the word they gave Moses: suited for battle with their brethren before returning to enjoy their own land on the other side.

On that day the Lord magnified Joshua in the sight of all Israel, and they feared him as they feared Moses all the days of his life. A man through whom the Lord makes a whole river stand up commands that reverence.

The priests stayed firm at their post in the riverbed even after all the people had passed over, until the Lord spake to Joshua and Joshua gave the order: come ye up out of Jordan. That is discipline, order, fortitude, and faith; they held their place in the midst of a stopped river without wavering.

As soon as the soles of the priests' feet were lifted up unto the dry land, the waters of Jordan returned unto their place and flowed over all his banks as they did before. Everything held its place exactly as long as Israel needed it to.
The people came up out of Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and encamped in Gilgal, in the east border of Jericho, and there Joshua pitched the twelve stones they took out of Jordan.

The fathers were given the answer for their children: Israel came over this Jordan on dry land, for the Lord your God dried up the waters of Jordan from before you until ye were passed over, as the Lord your God did to the Red Sea. The later generation witnessed the same kind of miracle the previous generation saw, because Joshua carried the same spirit Moses had, and the Lord rocked with him the same way.

The purpose is written: that all the people of the earth might know the hand of the Lord, that it is mighty, that ye might fear the Lord your God for ever. The world was made for Israel's sake; the waters and everything else in the earth answer to what the Most High commands for his people, but when the Lord is not dwelling among Israel, that power is not there. Seeing what he does in the twinkling of an eye is faith building, and it teaches the fear of the Lord.
